lines.text: imagine to ourselves as specific quantities in clear and firm
outline, even if they are ideal values (so-called) such as
beauty or character or nobility of soul, belong nevertheless
to the sphere of the human. They are of this world. Their
radiance fades in the very acute distress which now grips
our hearts; they fail us in times of trouble, bitter sorrow and
sore temptation. And we surmise that the "light of life" is
something which lies beyond them, just as indescribable and
vague as that which hovers before the minds of all of us and
which the naïve man calls "luck"; no one can precisely say
what it is. Or again just as indescribable and vague as what
we mean when we speak of the fulfilment and fruition of our
being, of what we essentially are or what we wish to be and
ought to be and yet never are and of which we have only
the vaguest intuition! But is it not just that which Jesus
means when He promises us the light of life? He pre-
supposes that everyone longs for it. And the newness of His
message is only this: "I am it!" "I am the light of life!"
And now what this "light of life" is may be formulated
somewhat more plainly, in so far as we may express more
clearly what it means for our lives, however mysterious it
may be. Why is it that this thing which we long for, without
knowing clearly its nature, is called the "light of life"? Light
is the power of illumination bringing clarity of vision so that
in consequence we walk "in the light" and do not grope in
darkness, uncertain of the way. Hence the "light of life"
would mean that life for us gains transparent clarity, that
the oppressive problems, the torturing mysteries of our life
come to an end; that we are no longer afraid of what is to
come, of what threatens, that we are no longer strangers to
ourselves, that, so to speak, everything has become self-
explanatory. "In that day you will ask me no questions,"
says Jesus to His disciples when He promises them the joy
which no man can take from them (John 16: 23). No longer
to need to ask questions because our whole existence has
become full of light-that is what it means to have the "light
of life".
